title: Conformance verification for real-time output hooks and external tool-invoke semantics on onboarded models
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a deterministic conformance verification workflow that certifies newly onboarded LLM variants for real-time streaming output and correctness/robustness of external tool/function invocation semantics. This ticket scopes the engineering work to design and implement test harnesses, canary gating rules, and a publishing step that writes a machine-readable compatibility statement into the model performance catalog. The verification must exercise interleaved streaming and function call patterns, chunk boundary edge cases, partial failure/fallback behavior, and KV cache coherence across calls.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Conformance harness exists and runs in CI against a model snapshot in < 25 minutes
A2: Telemetry captures handshake success/failure, tool call integrity, chunk reassembly errors, and end-to-end latency percentiles
A3: Canary gating policy defined: models fail onboarding if function-call integrity < 99.5% or stream continuity errors > 0.5% on synthetic workload
A4: Compatibility statement JSON produced and uploaded to the performance catalog for certified model versions
A5: Rollout plan with automated fallback to pinned compatible variant exists for runtime-2.3
test_plan: Create synthetic workloads that mix: short-turn chat with immediate function calls, long-form streaming with mid-stream tool invocation, and backpressure scenarios
Implement handshake fuzzing: vary initial chunk sizes, inter-chunk timing, and malformed metadata headers
Run KV cache coherence checks by issuing repeated partial prompts that rely on previously cached tokens before and after function calls
Measure metrics: handshake_success_rate, function_call_return_integrity, chunk_reassembly_errors, p50/p95/p99 latency for handshake and function completion
Failure injection: simulate transient model worker restarts and assert graceful fallback to pinned variant with no data corruption
implementation_notes: Reuse existing streaming harness from ENG-62311 but add function-call validation layer that executes a configurable set of tool stubs (HTTP webhook, local process, DB-write) and asserts semantic integrity of responses

Add a 'compatibility' JSON schema for the performance catalog with fields: model_version, streaming: {handshake_semantics, chunking_guarantees}, function_calls: {call_frame_boundary, tool_serialization, retry_semantics}, and telemetry_links
Instrument runtime to emit a unique request lineage id across stream+tool call transitions for easier reassembly in dashboards
Expose a canary config that maps failing checks to blocking gates in the onboarding pipeline and to automatic rollback in Dedicated deployments
qa_checklist: Run harness against current golden model (qa-gold-v1) and verify all acceptance criteria pass
Introduce a regression test into the pre-merge job that fails on semantic diffs in function call outputs
Manual exploratory session: instrumented local dev cluster, invoke a mixed workload and confirm trace linkability across steps
Stakeholder sign-off: PM and Design review the compatibility statement wording and public-facing implications
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Run conformance harness as part of nightly validation for all candidate onboarding snapshots
Stage 2: Enable pre-release canary gating for models in staging; failures create a blocked flag in onboarding UI
Stage 3: After two consecutive nightly passes, publish compatibility JSON to performance catalog and mark model as certified for streaming+tooling
Stage 4: Monitor first-week traffic using a 5% traffic ring with automatic fallback to pinned variant on >1% customer-impacting errors
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: False negatives from flaky synthetic workloads. Mitigation: diversify seed corpora and run multiple randomized seeds per run
Risk: Performance overhead from additional instrumentation. Mitigation: sample telemetry in production; full traces only in canary and CI
Risk: Inconsistent serialization across tool stubs. Mitigation: centralize tool-stub implementations and include golden fixtures for each tool type
